body.rationale: Governing IPS status is ratified, per the brief, so hard breaches count. Four candidates have no hard breaches: inverse_volatility, resampled_efficient_frontier, black_litterman and cvar_minimization. Risk_parity breaches only the volatility floor (7.56% against 8%) and has a -20.3% drawdown. My order favours covariance-based methods and diversified books, in line with the late-cycle reasoning the paper found. 1) Inverse_volatility: no breaches, no tuned parameter and no return forecast. Its intra-category reviewer confirmed the arithmetic. Effective N is 14.8 and the drawdown is -22.9%. The reviews flag that about 43% sits in correlated credit and sovereign sleeves, and that is a real weakness. 2) Resampled_efficient_frontier: no breaches and breadth of 13.1. Averaging tames the estimation error that max_sharpe suffers from. Its weakness is a drawdown of -24.84%, only 16bp inside the limit, so compliance is fragile. 3) Risk_parity: a covariance-only method with a low drawdown of -20.3% and breadth of 14.3. Reviewers noted that the 14.3 measures capital dispersion, not risk dispersion. The small volatility shortfall can be fixed by blending. 4) Black_litterman: compliant with Sharpe 0.42 and effective N 5.7. Its prior is distorted by overlapping ETF AUM, and it relies on a stable stock-bond correlation. 5) Cvar_minimization: compliant, with the best backtest Sharpe at 0.74 and a -18.7% drawdown. It ranks last because the reviews show it is concentrated in 4 assets (effective N 2.9) and tuned to land exactly on the 8.00% volatility floor. Inverse_volatility beats it because it reaches compliance with 14.8 effective assets and no tuning, so the CIO can lean on it more safely. I rank myself nowhere. My own 1/N breaches the drawdown limit, and I do not argue otherwise. Bottom flag is market_cap_weight: it has a -40.6% drawdown, a CRO risk score of 0.80 and about 77% in equity. Its reviewers showed that ETF AUM is not a market portfolio and double-counts overlapping US style sleeves. It is also candid that it is only a diagnostic. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, whose orthogonality is useful in an ensemble even though it breaches the return, volatility and tracking-error limits.
